key_moments: Julian Quiñones opened the scoring for Mexico with a powerful drive in the 22nd minute.
Raúl Jiménez doubled Mexico's lead in the 31st minute after a combination with Quiñones.
Ecuador's John Yeboah hit the woodwork in the 18th minute, a rare clear chance for La Tri.
Piero Hincapié of Ecuador received a red card in stoppage time (90+5') following a VAR review.

standout_performers.reason: Scored the opening goal and assisted the second, earning Player of the Match.
Scored Mexico's second goal and contributed to the team's attacking pressure.
Expertly marshalled the defense, contributing to Mexico's fourth consecutive clean sheet.
Led Ecuador's midfield with 57 accurate passes and created a big chance.

matches.tactical_summary: Mexico started with high intensity, securing two early goals through clinical finishing and effective counter-pressing. After establishing their lead, they adopted a more controlled defensive approach, absorbing Ecuador's possession without conceding significant threats.

narrative: Co-hosts Mexico delivered a dominant performance to defeat Ecuador 2-0, ending a 40-year drought for a knockout stage victory at the World Cup. Their fast start and impenetrable defense secured their passage, delighting the home crowd at Mexico City Stadium.
next_round_notes: Mexico advances to the Round of 16 with no reported injury or card concerns for their squad. Ecuador's Piero Hincapié will face a suspension following his late red card, though Ecuador has been eliminated from the tournament.
